findings.title: Terminal migration has no mint-free escape hatch if phUSD minter rights are revoked mid-migration
findings.triageReason: Intended design (user triage 2026-06-08, via /review-finding ss7m3). emergencyWithdraw/withdraw/deposit are deliberately frozen once migrationInfo[token].active because initiateMigration captures an immutable (R,P) snapshot and every exit pays a fixed pro-rata credit p_i*min(R,P)/P; a live exit during migration would mutate P and corrupt the snapshot (StableStaker.sol:306-307, 335-340). The Law-2 'faithfulness gap' framing is therefore invalid. The residual 'revoke staker's phUSD minter while migration active -> exits revert' sliver is an obvious admin misstep (Law 3 out-of-scope) and recoverable. Not submittable.
findings.proposalResolution: REJECTED 2026-06-08 — finding triaged wont-fix as intended design; proposed Medium not applied.
findings.description: During an active terminal migration, emergencyWithdraw is blocked (migration active), and the only exits (userMigrate, batchMigrate) mint frozen pending phUSD via _exitPosition -> phUSD.mint BEFORE transferring principal. If the staker loses phUSD minter rights while a token is active, those exits revert on the pending-phUSD mint and principal is retrievable only after minter rights are restored. Healthy mode has a mint-free escape (emergencyWithdraw); terminal mode does not. Bounded by the owner-trusted precondition 'minter revoked mid-migration'.
findings.impact: Owner-trust-bounded availability: principal is not permanently lost, but is temporarily unrecoverable from terminal-migration exits until phUSD minter rights are restored.

findings.title: finalizeAndReset revives pool without resetting phusdPerSecond / re-wiring yieldStrategy (revival over-emission footgun)
findings.description: story-009's finalizeAndReset flips poolState Migrating -> Active to revive a fully-drained pool, clearing the migration snapshot and fast-forwarding lastRewardTime, but it does NOT reset phusdPerSecond nor re-wire/clear yieldStrategy. A pool revived without re-configuring its emission rate / strategy resumes on stale settings: the prior phusdPerSecond is re-applied to fresh deposits, and the decoupled (or stale) strategy reference may not match operator intent. The per-second emission CAP is NOT violated and no principal is at risk; the hazard is that a non-obvious owner expectation (a 'reset' pool starts from a clean emission/strategy slate) does not hold.
findings.impact: Law-3 non-obvious owner-config footgun. The per-second emission CAP is NOT violated and no staked principal is at risk. The prior 'no principal is at risk' framing rested on the pre-story-023 premise that the reward token had no redemption path, and that premise is VOID for V2. Recommend finalizeAndReset zero antimatterPerSecond (or require explicit re-config) and clear/re-assert the yieldStrategy binding on revival.

findings.label: L-09
findings.title: Armed-but-near-empty pool keeps minting at the full scheduled rate: emission is TVL-independent, so a dust-sized position collects budgeted Antimatter that is now a claim on unbacked phUSD
findings.description: StableStakerV2 emits Antimatter on a pure TIME denominator: once a pool is non-empty, _updatePool computes reward = elapsed * antimatterPerSecond with no reference to totalStaked (totalStaked appears only at :824 as the divisor of the share index). An armed pool therefore keeps minting at its full scheduled rate even when the only position in it is dust, and the dust holder is the sole claimant of that stream while it stands alone. The pool does NOT bank anything while empty - the empty branch at :817-819 fast-forwards lastRewardTime and discards the window (see `retraction`).
findings.impact: Misallocation of BUDGETED emission, not net-new issuance and not a loss to any other staker. Since story-023 the emitted Antimatter is redeemable via the permissionless Antimatter.annihilate, which mints the antimatter half as unbacked phUSD, so misallocated emission does translate into a collateralization-ratio effect. Bounded by: emission stays inside the schedule; any genuine staker immediately dilutes the dust holder pro rata; and no staker is deprived of anything. LOW.

retraction.verdict: MECHANISM DISPROVED. The finding as filed claimed a dormant pool BANKS emissions that the first staker then captures. That is FALSE.
retraction.proof: _updatePool fast-forwards the clock on the empty branch (src/StableStakerV2.sol:816-819): `if (pool.totalStaked == 0) { pool.lastRewardTime = block.timestamp; return; }`. stake() calls _updatePool at :327 BEFORE `pool.totalStaked += credited` at :335, so at that moment the pool is still empty, lastRewardTime jumps to now, and the new staker's rewardDebt is set against an index that never advanced. The dormant window is DISCARDED, not banked. A staker entering after 10 idle days accrues only from that instant. This is textbook MasterChef and is correct behaviour.
retraction.pocMisreading: The PoC's 90-day warp occurred AFTER the 1-wei stake, so it only ever demonstrated that a SOLE staker holding dust collects the full rate GOING FORWARD - a narrower claim than the finding made. The companion test test_emptyPoolAccruesNothing measured lastRewardTime advancing with accAntimatterPerShare unchanged: that measurement WAS the refutation, and it was mis-read as supporting evidence.
retraction.whatSurvives: Emission is time-denominated and TVL-independent, so an armed pool with negligible stake still mints at the full scheduled rate, and since story-023 those tokens are claims on unbacked phUSD. Real, but bounded: no other staker is diluted out of anything; any genuine staker immediately dilutes the dust holder pro rata; and the tokens emitted are BUDGETED emission being MISALLOCATED, not issuance conjured outside the schedule.
retraction.notInflated: The ~$900k figure in the original report and PoC is the size of a 90-day scheduled emission budget, not net-new issuance and not a measure of loss.
